record.entity_title: Declaring a Latvian address alone makes you a tax resident
record.fact_text: Under the Law On Taxes and Fees a natural person is a Latvian tax resident if their declared place of residence is in Latvia OR they are present 183+ days in any 12-month period. Either limb is sufficient, so declaring a Riga address can make someone a full tax resident (taxed on worldwide income) before they ever reach the day-count.
record.evidence_quote: a natural person shall be considered a resident if: 1) the declared place of residence of this person is the Republic of Latvia; 2) this person stays in the Republic of Latvia for 183 days or longer during any 12 month period beginning or ending in a taxation year

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Most people assume tax residency is a 183-day test; in Latvia a declared address is an independent, equally sufficient trigger, so the mandatory HOUSING address declaration can create worldwide-income tax residency immediately.
